logp.method_description: The octanol/water partition coefficient, Po/w (or log Po/w), is a measure of the amphiphilicity of a material. It represents the relative solubilities of a given material in oil and water. The octanol/water partition coefficient Po/w of LIr1 was measured on an HY-4 oscillator according to a classical method. (17) Equal amounts of n-octanol and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) were thoroughly mixed in the oscillator for 24 h. The mixture was then left to separate for a further 24 h so as to yield water and octanol phases, each saturated with the other. Complex LIr1 was carefully dissolved in PBS (concentration denoted as Co) and PBS saturated with octanol to form a 20 μM solution. The latter was then mixed with an equal amount of octanol (saturated with water) and shaken again as described above. After separation, the final concentration of LIr1 in water was denoted as Cw. Both Co and Cw were measured by spectrophotometry at λ = 310 nm, and the partition coefficient (Po/w) for LIr1 was calculated according to the equation: Po/w = (Co – Cw)/Cw.
